subject: physical-education
title: Synthesis and review: peer feedback
essentialQuestion: How can understanding leadership, officiating, and inclusive participation help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?

lessonFamilyPlan.guidedEmphasis: Recall two named prior cues, re-model the less secure cue, and explain when each cue applies.

goal: I can retrieve prior cues and combine them in a fresh variation for peer feedback, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Direction, model, choice, feedback. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Turn one multi-action direction into two one-action cues.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: soft household markers or a written cue card.
Use spoken, signed, drawn, or imagined directions and boundaries.
movementCues: PREVIEW space, equipment, start, stop, and adaptation before activity.
MODEL one observable action or decision at a time.
OFFER seated, supported, reduced-demand, solo, and no-equipment choices before practice.
FEEDBACK names the cue or decision, never a body, ability, effort, or character.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Rehearse the model slowly, change one variable, and explain the cue or decision before adding complexity.

movementModel.title: Model for peer feedback

movementModel.action: State one direction, model or describe it slowly, offer equal-credit routes, and give one cue-based feedback sentence.
movementModel.commonError: Giving many directions at once or presenting adaptation only after a learner struggles.
movementModel.correction: Chunk one action, offer routes before practice, and rewrite feedback around an observable cue.
movementModel.notice: Notice clarity, consent, inclusion, and safe organization rather than compliance or athletic result.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice clarity, consent, inclusion, and safe organization rather than compliance or athletic result.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Use a solo plan or one trusted household partner only; consent and stop signals apply before any shared activity. No required partner, contact, public leadership, audience, spotting, lifting, or responsibility for another person’s safety decision.

guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Chunk one action, offer routes before practice, and rewrite feedback around an observable cue.

guidedPractice.prompt: Present one direction and one equal-credit choice to an imagined learner.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: peer feedback
directions: Create a fresh solo activity briefing with setup, model, adaptation, stop signal, and cue-based feedback.
Use this cue or decision: Direction, model, choice, feedback.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Use the retrieved cues in a varied example with no new untaught movement. Create a fresh solo activity briefing with setup, model, adaptation, stop signal, and cue-based feedback.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Rehearse the opening and stop signals.
Model one target cue slowly from a stable position.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Use a safe seat or one arm-span. A team, public role, audience, contact, spotting, lifting, or real event is not required. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: soft household markers or a written cue card.
householdSubstitutes: Use spoken, signed, drawn, or imagined directions and boundaries.
prohibited: No required partner, contact, public leadership, audience, spotting, lifting, or responsibility for another person’s safety decision.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit solo route: design and speak, sign, write, or demonstrate the opening cue, setup, adaptation, feedback statement, and stop signal; no partner or audience is required.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Use a solo plan or one trusted household partner only; consent and stop signals apply before any shared activity.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Direction, model, choice, feedback. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for peer feedback, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for peer feedback.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Direction, model, choice, feedback. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit solo route: design and speak, sign, write, or demonstrate the opening cue, setup, adaptation, feedback statement, and stop signal; no partner or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit solo route: design and speak, sign, write, or demonstrate the opening cue, setup, adaptation, feedback statement, and stop signal; no partner or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Create a fresh solo activity briefing with setup, model, adaptation, stop signal, and cue-based feedback. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

accessibleAdaptation: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice clarity, consent, inclusion, and safe organization rather than compliance or athletic result. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit solo route: design and speak, sign, write, or demonstrate the opening cue, setup, adaptation, feedback statement, and stop signal; no partner or audience is required.
activitySteps: Choose a standard or equal-credit response route.
Read the STOP AND TELL rule.
Complete the warm-up when it applies.
Use the safe finish when it applies.
Answer the short reflection or leave it blank.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Giving many directions at once or presenting adaptation only after a learner struggles.

learnerEvidence: One guided response using Direction, model, choice, feedback..
One fresh bounded application or complete described equivalent for peer feedback.
One cue, decision, safety, or next-step explanation.
evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.
doNotCollect: weight, appearance, body composition, calories, body shape, fitness norms, speed versus peers, or athletic talent
diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for peer feedback; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Turn one multi-action direction into two one-action cues.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Direction, model, choice, feedback.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Giving many directions at once or presenting adaptation only after a learner struggles. — with this correction — Chunk one action, offer routes before practice, and rewrite feedback around an observable cue.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Present one direction and one equal-credit choice to an imagined learner.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Create a fresh solo activity briefing with setup, model, adaptation, stop signal, and cue-based feedback. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice clarity, consent, inclusion, and safe organization rather than compliance or athletic result. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.

coach how the learner presents their own evidence
route to rest, stop, retry, or adult handoff
mustNot: cannot diagnose, prescribe, rehabilitate, or give medical clearance
cannot claim unapproved observation or certify physical completion
cannot override rest, stop, adaptation, guardian authority, professional authority, or safe return
cannot choose the answer or action for fresh independent evidence

keyPoints: Use a solo planning station with the opening cue, boundary, stop signal, and adaptation choices visible.
State one direction, model or describe it slowly, offer equal-credit routes, and give one cue-based feedback sentence.
Chunk one action, offer routes before practice, and rewrite feedback around an observable cue.
privacySafeScenario: Use a supplied or invented non-personal example of peer feedback; do not disclose private health information or recreate a hazard.
studentTask: Use the retrieved cues in a varied example with no new untaught movement. Create a fresh solo activity briefing with setup, model, adaptation, stop signal, and cue-based feedback. Use any approved standard or equal-credit route. Name the cue or decision that controlled the result; no body metric, comparison, recording, or physical-completion claim is required.
knowledgeCheck: State the starting position, action, key cue, common error, and correction for peer feedback. Then distinguish optional REST / ADJUST from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME.
completionCriteria: The learner uses a safe setup or accurately describes it for peer feedback.
The learner applies Direction, model, choice, feedback. in one guided attempt and one fresh application or complete described equivalent.
The learner distinguishes learner-controlled rest from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME conditions.
Any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route earns equal credit for the same cue or decision evidence.
adaptationChoices: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice clarity, consent, inclusion, and safe organization rather than compliance or athletic result. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
extensionChallenge: Apply peer feedback under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

optionalReflection.prompt: Which cue, decision, safety check, or adaptation preserved the target for peer feedback, and what would you keep or change in a next safe attempt?

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
